# Tobit Chapter 8 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 8 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_008_page_001.jpg

---

**1** After the meal was over, they brought Tobias to Sarah's room.

**2** On his way in, he remembered what Raphael had told him. He took the incense ashes and laid the fish's heart and liver on top of them, then let the smoke rise.

**3** The demon caught the smell and fled all the way to the far reaches of Egypt. Raphael followed him there and bound him — chained for good.

**4** Once they were alone together, Tobias got up from the bed and said, "Come, my sister — let us pray together that the Lord will have mercy on us."

**5** Tobias began to pray: "Blessed are you, O God of our ancestors, and blessed is your name forever and ever. May the heavens praise you, and all your creation, for all ages to come.

**6** You made Adam, and you gave him Eve to be his companion and strength. From the two of them came every human being who has ever lived. You said yourself, 'It is not good for a man to be alone — I will make him someone to stand beside him.'

**7** And now, Lord, I am not taking this woman as my wife because of physical desire. I am doing this honestly, with a true heart. Have mercy on both of us, and let us grow old together."

**8** Together they both said, "Amen. Amen."

**9** And they slept. Meanwhile, Raguel got up and went outside — and dug a grave.

**10** He told himself, "What if this one dies too?" Then he went back inside

**11** and said to his wife Edna, "Send one of the slave girls to check on them. If he's dead, let's bury him quietly before anyone finds out."

**12** The girl slipped into the room — and found them both fast asleep.

**13** She came back out and told them: he was alive.

**14** Raguel burst out in praise to God: "Blessed are you, O God — all pure and holy blessing belongs to you! May your holy ones praise you, and all your creatures and angels and chosen people — may they praise you forever!

**15** Blessed are you, because you have given me joy — my worst fear has not come true. You have been so much more merciful to us than we deserved.

**16** Blessed are you, because you have had mercy on these two young people who are all each other had. Lord, show them mercy now. Give them health, give them joy, give them love and happiness in their lives.

**17** Give them long years together, Lord — full of gladness."

**18** Then Raguel ordered his servants to fill in the grave before sunrise.

**19** He told Edna to bake a mountain of bread, and he went to the flocks himself and brought back two bulls and four rams and set the men to work slaughtering and preparing them.

**20** He took Tobias aside and made him swear: "You are not leaving here for two weeks.

**21** You will stay here with me — eating, drinking, celebrating — and you will lift my daughter's spirit, because she has been through so much. Then take half of everything I own and go back to your father in peace. The other half will be yours when Edna and I are gone. You are our son now, Tobias — as much as Sarah is our daughter. This is your home. Take heart."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

Chapter 8 is the emotional and theological heart of the Book of Tobit. The wedding night prayer is not just beautiful — it reframes the entire story as being about covenant faithfulness rather than magic or adventure.

- **Verses 2-3**: The exorcism is vivid and strange. PNEUMA leans into that strangeness: the smell driving a demon across continents, Raphael in pursuit. The scene asks the reader to trust without over-explaining.
- **Verse 7**: This is the crux. Tobias explicitly renounces lust as his motive. PNEUMA renders this as "physically desire" / "honestly, with a true heart" — the contrast should be felt, not just understood. "True heart" captures ep' aletheias better than a bare "in truth."
- **Verse 9**: Raguel digging a grave on his daughter's wedding night is one of the most heartbreaking moments in the book. PNEUMA places it as a standalone beat — "and dug a grave" — with nothing softening it.
- **Verse 14**: Raguel's doxology erupts from relief. PNEUMA renders it with energy ("burst out in praise") to reflect the emotional release after hours of dread.
- **Verse 21**: The adoption language is made explicit — "you are our son now." The legal texture of the original is preserved but humanized.

*— PNEUMA*
